name: Mii head replacement state
notes: Mii head state is separate from the selected character ID.
This field is written while selected character ID is 0x52 / Mii.
The first observed write during Mii selection wrote value 0, so this should not yet be treated as a simple boolean enabled flag.
It may be a Mii head index, Mii slot, or replacement-state field.

values.meaning: observed value written when selecting Mii; exact meaning unknown
previously suspected Mii head replacement enabled value; unconfirmed

observations.summary: The value written to select-state +0x3C comes from local_4c. local_48 is then classified by character ID range around 0x52-0x59.
observations.pseudocode: *(selectState + playerOffset + 0x3C) = local_4c; if (local_48 - 0x52 < 8) { if (local_48 - 0x54 < 2) category = 0; else if (local_48 - 0x52 < 6) category = 3; else category = 1; } else category = 2;

observations.summary: Category 0 and category 3 both call FUN_800CD690 four times. Category 1 calls it two times. Category 2 appears to skip this call path. FUN_800CD690 adjusts r3 and tail-branches to FUN_800F7E98, which consumes the apparent index/value arguments.

category_behavior.behavior: call FUN_800CD690 four times; includes 0x52 / Mii

observations.pseudocode: FUN_800F7E98(param_1, param_2, param_3, param_4) { *(param_1 + param_2 * 0xC4 + param_3 * 4 + 8) = param_4; }
observations.summary: FUN_800CD690 is a base-adjusting tail-call wrapper. FUN_800F7E98 performs the indexed write, so local_80[index] is applied there.

open_questions: Determine what local_4c represents before it is written to select-state +0x3C.
Determine whether 0x808A2260 is a Mii head index, a replacement toggle, or another Mii state field.
Identify the meaning of the local_48 character category values 0, 1, 2, and 3.
Compare writes to 0x808A2260 for normal characters versus CHAR_ID_MII.
Find the function that commits Mii head state alongside selected character and costume.
Determine whether values other than 0 and 1 select Mii head variants or are invalid.
